titleEn: The Ducks Are Home—Time for Sleep!

pages.text: "I'm not going to bed yet!" Little pig Dingding, wearing a crimson apron, stacked empty bamboo baskets in the yard. In the paddy below, ducks filed into their house. Dingding swallowed a yawn. "Just one more basket!"
Mom, who worked several paddies on her own, came to the doorway with a lantern. "Dingding, the ducks are home. It's bedtime." "I'm not sleepy at all!" Dingding hugged the tower of baskets.
But Dingding's eyelids kept drooping. A basket slipped out of their hands and fell with a thump. Dingding's mouth opened in a big yawn. "Oh! Maybe I'm a little sleepy..."

Grandma, who had farmed rice all her life, came into the yard. "Look at the paddy below." The last duck wagged its tail and slipped into the duck house. Grandma sang, "The Ducks Are Home—Time for Sleep!"

"First, brush your teeth!" Grandma put a toothbrush in her mouth and brushed side to side. Dingding brushed by the basin in the yard, with bubbles around their mouth. They looked at each other and giggled.
Second, snuggle under the blanket! In the room, Dingding pulled the blanket up to their chin. Mom bent down, kissed Dingding's forehead, and sang softly, "The Ducks Are Home—Time for Sleep!"

Third, blow out the lamp! A thin strip of moonlight came through the door, so the dark room was not scary. Grandma lay beside Dingding and patted gently. "The Ducks Are Home—Time for Sleep!" Her voice was as warm as paddy water warmed by the day's sun.

Now it was Dingding's turn. Dingding sang into Mom's ear, "The Ducks Are Home—Time for Sleep!" Dingding sniffed. The night smelled cool. "I can stack baskets again tomorrow." Their eyes slowly closed.

The next evening, Dingding got under the blanket first. "One, stop playing when the ducks go home! Two, brush and get into bed! Three, when the lamp goes out, go to sleep!" All three closed their eyes side by side. The duck house and the room were quiet, with only soft breathing to be heard.

Morning came. The ducks poured out into the paddy, quacking. Dingding stretched in the doorway, and Mom gave them a big hug. "You slept so well all night!" An early bedtime made the morning feel fresh. "The Ducks Are Home—Time for Sleep!"
